evals.prompt: I want to set up an automated release pipeline for my app. The plan is: push to internal first, then after 2 days move to alpha at 100%, then after 7 days go to production at 10%, and after 14 days complete the rollout to 100%. I also want it to stop automatically if crash rate goes above 1.5% or ANR rate above 0.5%. How do I configure this with gpc?
evals.expected_output: Shows the full .gpcrc-train.json config (top-level stages and gates) and the gpc train start command
expectations: Provides a .gpcrc-train.json file with 4 stages: internal@100, alpha@100 after 2d, production@10 after 7d, production@100 after 14d
Includes gates config with crashes.max: 1.5 and anr.max: 0.5
Shows gpc train start to kick off the pipeline
Mentions gpc train status for checking progress
Explains that gate checks happen automatically before each stage transition

evals.prompt: My release train stopped progressing and I'm not sure why. It was on stage 3 — production at 10% — and it was supposed to move to 100% two days ago but nothing happened. How do I find out what went wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains the likely causes (advance not scheduled, gate breach, no gate data) and how to diagnose and restart
expectations: Suggests running gpc train status to see the train status (running or paused) and stage times
Explains that a crash or ANR rate above the configured gate threshold will pause progression
Shows gpc vitals crashes and gpc vitals anr to check current metric values against configured thresholds
Explains that the user must fix the regression (new release) and then restart with gpc train start --force (there is no resume command)
Mentions that gpc train advance must actually run (on a schedule) and that the after delay must have elapsed; a gate with no data holds the train with TRAIN_GATE_NO_DATA

evals.prompt: We found a critical crash affecting a large percentage of users on our latest release. The release train is currently at stage 3 — production at 10% rollout. We need to stop everything immediately. What's the fastest way to kill the train and halt the rollout?
evals.expected_output: Halts the rollout with gpc releases rollout halt, then aborts the train, and explains that abort alone does not stop users getting the release
expectations: Shows gpc releases rollout halt --track production as the first command, because it is what stops the rollout
Explains that abort only clears the train state and does not halt rollouts; halting needs gpc releases rollout halt --track <track>
Distinguishes abort (clears state) from gpc train pause (stops advance); neither halts the rollout on Google Play
Suggests gpc vitals crashes --dim versionCode to investigate the regression after aborting
Then shows gpc train abort (or pause) so a scheduled gpc train advance cannot move the release forward again

evals.prompt: How do I check which stage my release train is currently on and whether the gates are healthy?
evals.expected_output: Shows gpc train status with a description of the output format
expectations: Shows gpc train status as the primary command
Describes the output: status, current stage index, each stage with executedAt or scheduledAt, and the configured gates
Explains that status does not show live gate values; checks gpc vitals crashes and gpc vitals anr against the gates (gate max values are percentages)
Explains how to work out when the next stage is eligible from the current stage executedAt plus the next stage after delay
Notes that gpc status (without train) can confirm rollout percentages on each track match the active stage
